model.status: Requested through the authorized ChatGPT subscription CLI in the first Reactor Lab development pilot.

limits.note: Initial generous development ceilings, not calibrated main-run limits. Stop on completion. Record official 1000-step and extended 2000-step outcomes separately. No aggregate reported-token cutoff; record input/output/cached tokens. Preserve intrinsic model context limits.

source_validation: Authoring only; no new world executions or scientific confirmation
freeze: The model-authored source bundle is copied before any target is opened. No method or prompt changes during this registered pair of targets; keep every attempt.
pairing: Both agents start each fresh official seed from zero observations with the same source program and separate prior-world archive, model, tools and resource ceilings. No old object bindings, questions or supported answers are restored. Each agent chooses whether to use, adapt or ignore the supplied source.
scope: Two of the previously registered evaluation tasks, not new development seeds or the full panel. Tests same-experience organization and actual transferred-program adoption. No archive-deletion arm: this does not identify the incremental causal value of memory. A later edited target program is adaptation, not unchanged frozen execution.

outcomes.primary: Environment completedSuccessfully at the fixed action limits, macro averaged by theme and difficulty.
secondary: successful experiments and revised hypotheses in actual action traces
model calls, tokens including cached input, elapsed/model/Python time
service, timeout, invalid action, budget exhaustion and scientific failure categories
outcomes.knowledge_score: Official free-text explanatory-knowledge score requires a judge. Do not substitute success/procedural score for it; no knowledge-accuracy claim until a judging protocol is specified.

fairness: Both agents receive the same public text observations/actions and initial files. Ordinary Code can store and execute its own research programs. Gold rules, hidden scorecards and scenario source are evaluation-side materials.
